title: John Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 1.

questions.question: In the beginning, what was with God?
questions.explanation: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. (John 1:1)

questions.question: How were all things made?
questions.explanation: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. (John 1:3)

questions.question: What was the life in Him described as?
questions.explanation: In him was life; and the life was the light of men. (John 1:4)

questions.question: True or False: John was sent from God.
questions.explanation: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. (John 1:6)

questions.question: What did John come to do?
options: To bear witness of the Light
questions.correctAnswer: To bear witness of the Light
questions.explanation: The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe. (John 1:7)

questions.question: True or False: John was the Light.
questions.explanation: He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. (John 1:8)

questions.question: Who is referred to as the true Light?
questions.explanation: That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world. (John 1:9)

questions.question: In John 1, which instruction comes first?
options: All things were made by Him
questions.correctAnswer: All things were made by Him
questions.explanation: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. (John 1:3)

questions.question: True or False: Many received Him and were given power to become the sons of God.
questions.explanation: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name. (John 1:12)

questions.question: What was the condition for being born of God?
options: Not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man
questions.correctAnswer: Not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man
questions.explanation: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. (John 1:13)

questions.question: The Word was made flesh and dwelt among whom?
questions.explanation: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us. (John 1:14)

questions.question: True or False: The law was given by Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ. (John 1:17)

medium.title: John Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to John 1:18, who has declared God?
questions.explanation: The only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him. This shows that Jesus reveals God to us (John 1:18).

questions.question: What was John the Baptist's role as described in John 1:23?
options: The voice of one crying in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of one crying in the wilderness
questions.explanation: John identified himself as the voice of one crying in the wilderness, fulfilling the prophecy (John 1:23).

questions.question: In John 1:29, what title does John the Baptist give to Jesus?
questions.explanation: John refers to Jesus as the Lamb of God, emphasizing His role in taking away the sin of the world (John 1:29).

questions.question: True or False: John the Baptist claimed to be the Christ.
questions.explanation: John confessed that he was not the Christ, indicating his role was to prepare the way for Jesus (John 1:20).

questions.question: What did John say would happen to those who believe in Jesus according to John 1:12?
options: They will become the sons of God
questions.correctAnswer: They will become the sons of God
questions.explanation: John states that to those who receive Him, He gives the power to become the sons of God (John 1:12).

questions.question: What does John 1:33 say about the one who baptizes with the Holy Ghost?
options: He is the Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: He is the Son of God
questions.explanation: John identifies Jesus, the one who baptizes with the Holy Ghost, as the Son of God (John 1:34).

questions.question: According to John 1:25, why did the priests and Levites question John the Baptist?
options: To inquire why he was baptizing
questions.correctAnswer: To inquire why he was baptizing
questions.explanation: They questioned him about his authority to baptize since he was not the Christ or a prophet (John 1:25).

questions.question: True or False: John the Baptist was sent by God.
questions.explanation: The text states that there was a man sent from God, whose name was John, confirming his divine mission (John 1:6).

questions.question: What was the significance of the Spirit descending like a dove, as mentioned in John 1:32?
questions.explanation: The descending of the Spirit like a dove indicated the anointing of Jesus for His ministry (John 1:32).

questions.question: What did Nathanael proclaim about Jesus in John 1:49?
options: He is the Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: He is the Son of God
questions.explanation: Nathanael recognized Jesus as the Son of God and the King of Israel (John 1:49).

questions.question: What does John 1:30 reveal about Jesus in relation to John the Baptist?
options: Jesus was a disciple of John
questions.explanation: John acknowledges that Jesus, who comes after him, is preferred before him because He existed before John (John 1:30).

questions.question: What does John 1:31 indicate about John's knowledge of Jesus?
options: He was always aware of Him
He did not know Him initially
questions.correctAnswer: He did not know Him initially
questions.explanation: John admits that he did not know Jesus until He was made manifest to Israel (John 1:31).

hard.title: John Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 1.

questions.question: What title does John the Baptist use to refer to Jesus when he sees Him coming?
questions.explanation: John refers to Jesus as 'the Lamb of God' in John 1:29, highlighting His role in taking away the sin of the world, a concept echoed in Isaiah 53:7, where the suffering servant is likened to a lamb led to slaughter.

questions.question: Which disciple is specifically mentioned as the brother of Simon Peter in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Andrew is introduced as Simon Peter's brother in John 1:40, indicating his significant role in bringing others to Christ.

questions.question: Jesus tells Nathanael that he will see greater things than being seen under the fig tree. What does Jesus refer to that he will see?
questions.explanation: In John 1:51, Jesus indicates that Nathanael will witness greater revelations, specifically referencing the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man, reminiscent of Jacob's dream in Genesis 28:12.

questions.question: Who sent priests and Levites to question John the Baptist?
questions.explanation: John 1:24 states that the individuals questioning John were of the Pharisees, highlighting their role in religious leadership and scrutiny during that time.

questions.question: What does John the Baptist say he baptizes with?
questions.explanation: In John 1:26, John the Baptist explicitly states, 'I baptize with water,' contrasting his baptism with that of Jesus, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What does the term 'Messias' mean as used by Andrew when he finds Simon?
questions.explanation: Andrew tells Simon that they have found the 'Messias' in John 1:41, which translates to 'the Anointed One,' signifying Jesus' role as the Christ, fulfilling the Old Testament prophecy of an anointed deliverer.

questions.question: In John 1:46, what was Nathanael's initial reaction to Nazareth?
questions.explanation: Nathanael expresses skepticism about whether any good can come from Nazareth in John 1:46, reflecting the low regard some had for that town.

questions.question: What does Jesus declare about Nathanael when He sees him coming?
options: He is an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile
questions.correctAnswer: He is an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile
questions.explanation: Jesus acknowledges Nathanael's integrity by calling him 'an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile' in John 1:47, indicating His divine knowledge of Nathanael's character.

questions.question: What significant event occurs when John the Baptist sees Jesus?
options: He declares Him as the Lamb of God
questions.correctAnswer: He declares Him as the Lamb of God
questions.explanation: Upon seeing Jesus, John the Baptist proclaims, 'Behold the Lamb of God' in John 1:29, announcing Jesus' mission to take away the sins of humanity.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Jesus is TRUE, according to John 1:12?
options: All received Him became sons of God
He came only for the Jews
He rejected those who did not believe
questions.correctAnswer: All received Him became sons of God
questions.explanation: John 1:12 states that 'as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God,' emphasizing the acceptance and transformative relationship with Christ.

questions.question: In John 1:17, what does the text say came by Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: John 1:17 indicates that 'grace and truth came by Jesus Christ,' contrasting with the law given by Moses, highlighting the new covenant established through Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: John the Baptist identified himself as the Christ.
questions.explanation: In John 1:20, John the Baptist explicitly denies being the Christ, clarifying his role as a witness to the Light.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was called the King of Israel by Nathanael.
questions.explanation: Nathanael recognizes Jesus as 'the Son of God' and 'the King of Israel' in John 1:49, affirming Jesus' royal and divine identity.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in John 1:1-5, reflecting the duality of Christ's nature?
questions.explanation: The use of contrasting ideas in John 1:1-5, such as light versus darkness, exemplifies antithesis, highlighting the nature of Christ as both divine and present in the world.

theological.title: John Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of Christ is revealed in John 1:1?
questions.explanation: John 1:1 reveals that 'the Word was with God, and the Word was God,' affirming the doctrine of Christ's divinity.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by the statement 'In him was life' in John 1:4?
questions.explanation: John 1:4 states, 'In him was life,' illustrating God's attribute of being the source of life.

questions.question: What does John 1:12 teach about the process of becoming children of God?
questions.explanation: John 1:12 states that those who receive Him are given the power to become sons of God, emphasizing faith as the means.

questions.question: How does John 1:14 contribute to our understanding of the Incarnation?
questions.explanation: John 1:14 declares, 'And the Word was made flesh,' signifying the Incarnation of Christ.

questions.question: What combined teaching do John 1:9 and John 1:10 convey about Christ's relationship with the world?
options: He created the world but was not known by it
questions.correctAnswer: He created the world but was not known by it
questions.explanation: John 1:9 states He is the true Light, and John 1:10 notes the world was made by Him, yet did not know Him.

questions.question: What is the significance of John the Baptist's role as described in John 1:7?
options: To bear witness of the Light
questions.correctAnswer: To bear witness of the Light
questions.explanation: John 1:7 indicates that John was sent to bear witness of the Light so that all might believe through him.

questions.question: In John 1:17, what distinction is made between the law and grace?
options: The law and grace are the same
questions.explanation: John 1:17 contrasts the law given by Moses with the grace and truth that came through Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What does John 1:22 reveal about the expectations of the priests and Levites?
options: They wanted to know John's identity
They were not interested in John's ministry
questions.correctAnswer: They wanted to know John's identity
questions.explanation: In John 1:22, the priests and Levites ask John about his identity, reflecting their expectation for a significant figure.

questions.question: What is the apologetic response to the sceptics' claim that Jesus was just a man and not divine?
questions.explanation: John 1:1 explicitly states 'the Word was God,' directly addressing the claim of Jesus' divinity.

questions.question: What does John 1:34 affirm about Jesus' identity?
options: He is the Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: He is the Son of God
questions.explanation: John 1:34 states, 'I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God,' affirming Jesus' divine sonship.

questions.question: What narrative arc does John 1:29 provide regarding Jesus' mission?
options: He came to heal the sick
He is the Lamb of God who takes away sin
He is a teacher of the law
He came to establish a kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: He is the Lamb of God who takes away sin
questions.explanation: John 1:29 identifies Jesus as 'the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world,' highlighting His redemptive purpose.

questions.question: What does John 1:46 reveal about Nathanael's initial reaction to Jesus?
questions.explanation: In John 1:46, Nathanael expresses skepticism, asking, 'Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?'

questions.question: How do John 1:39 and John 1:40 together illustrate the call of the disciples?
questions.explanation: John 1:39 shows Jesus inviting them to 'Come and see,' which leads to John 1:40 where one of them seeks to bring his brother to Jesus.

questions.question: What attribute of God is suggested by the phrase 'full of grace and truth' in John 1:14?
questions.explanation: John 1:14 describes Jesus as 'full of grace and truth,' indicating God's attribute of grace in His character.

questions.question: What does John 1:51 foreshadow about the future revelation of Jesus?
questions.explanation: John 1:51 indicates that they will see 'heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man,' foreshadowing Christ's future revelation.
